blocks.text: Day 5 · Transfer by bus to Puerto Natales (approx. 5 hours) across the vast Patagonian landscape, with the mountain ranges creating an amazing backdrop for your journey. Puerto Natales is a charming fishing town on the shore of the Almirante Montt Gulf, a seemingly endless stretch of deep blue water. Spend the evening strolling among its low-rise houses and colourful façades.

blocks.text:
Day 6 · Full-day shared tour to Torres del Paine National Park, the highlight of Chilean Patagonia. The day begins at the Milodón Cave on Cerro Benítez, 25 km from Puerto Natales, where the remains of a sabre-toothed cat, a native horse and a giant ground sloth, the mylodon, were discovered in 1895. Walk for about 30 minutes through the cave among its stalactite formations.

The landscape changes from Magellanic forest to windswept Patagonian plains; inside the park appear dozens of lakes full of birds, crystal-clear blue waters, waterfalls and ice-capped peaks. A 15-minute walk leads to Salto Grande, the waterfall linking Lakes Nordenskjöld and Pehoé, and the return follows a beautiful road past the Serrano River and Lakes Toro and Porteño.

Among the many possible hikes, one takes you to the foot of the world-famous Towers, along mountain paths, over bridges and babbling brooks and through verdant woodland, perhaps with a condor soaring overhead, up to an emerald lake beneath the three granite peaks. Your transfer then takes you back to your hotel.
A wide, dark entrance to Milodón Cave beneath an overhanging rock, Chile
